questions.explanation: In-context learning, the headline finding of the GPT-3 paper, means the model learns the task from demonstrations in the prompt alone.

questions.prompt: According to Min et al. (2022), which aspects of demonstrations drive performance? Select all that apply.

options.text: The label space (which answers are allowed)
Using as many examples as will fit

questions.explanation: Randomly replacing labels barely hurt performance; the label space, input distribution, and format were the key drivers. More examples can actually cause overfitting.

questions.prompt: Prompting with several examples of input and desired output before the real input is called ____-shot prompting.
questions.explanation: Few-shot (or multi-shot) prompting includes several examples; one-shot has one, and zero-shot has none.

questions.prompt: Your few-shot sentiment prompt has three POSITIVE examples, one NEUTRAL, and no NEGATIVE. What's the most likely problem?

options.text: The model will refuse to answer
The model may rarely or never answer NEGATIVE and over-predict POSITIVE
The prompt will exceed the context window

questions.explanation: Examples define the label space and can bias predictions. Cover every label, balance them, and vary the order.

questions.prompt: Order these steps for improving a few-shot prompt.

items.text: Add examples targeting the cases it got wrong
Test on real inputs with shuffled example order
Retest to confirm the fixes held

questions.explanation: Begin with a small, balanced set, test it (including order sensitivity), target the failures with new examples, and retest.

questions.prompt: Match each approach to when it fits best.

pairs.right: Locking in an exact output format
Consistent labels, tone, and fuzzy boundaries
Rare edge cases with a large context budget

questions.explanation: More examples buy consistency and coverage at the cost of length, latency, and overfitting risk.
